content: Why does the abbrev docs#Subspace exist? It is an abbrevation for Submodule for [DivisionRing R]. Should we just remove it? There are 69 declarations using it.
Gosh, docs#FiniteDimensional.LinearEquiv.quotEquivOfEquiv doesn't look like a good def
It appears that this is something that was ported from Mathlib 3. I think we should refactor to remove it.
I think it existed to match abbrev VectorSpace, which it seems we removed.
But it would be good to find the PR that did that to confirm

From the top of my head, back in Lean 3 days, having vector_space as an abbrev for module that took a field gave typeclass issues, which subspace didn't. So vector_space got removed as an active source of harm, and subspace was kept as harmless.
I'm happy to remove Subspace, since it seems unlikely to help anything over Submodule + Field.

Eric Wieser said:

But it would be good to find the PR that did that to confirm

Found it: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/pull/7322
